# Data model

## 1. Security data lake (OCSF-flat)

Every event becomes one row of a single wide, typed table. Files are Parquet (zstd), written under
`events/cls=<class_uid>/dt=<YYYY-MM-DD>/hr=<HH>/<batch-hash>.parquet` (UTC). `cls`, `dt` and `hr` are partition
columns used for pruning by DuckDB, Athena (partition projection) and the ADX ingestion mapping.

### OCSF classes

| class_uid | Class |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | ('Base Event', 'Uncategorized') |
| 1001 | ('File System Activity', 'System Activity') |
| 1007 | ('Process Activity', 'System Activity') |
| 2004 | ('Detection Finding', 'Findings') |
| 3001 | ('Account Change', 'Identity & Access Management') |
| 3002 | ('Authentication', 'Identity & Access Management') |
| 3005 | ('User Access Management', 'Identity & Access Management') |
| 4001 | ('Network Activity', 'Network Activity') |
| 4002 | ('HTTP Activity', 'Network Activity') |
| 4003 | ('DNS Activity', 'Network Activity') |
| 4009 | ('Email Activity', 'Network Activity') |
| 6003 | ('API Activity', 'Application Activity') |

### Columns

| Column | Arrow type | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `time` | timestamp[ms, tz=UTC] | event time (UTC) |
| `class_uid` | int32 | OCSF class id, e.g. 3002 Authentication |
| `class_name` | string | OCSF class name |
| `activity_name` | string | OCSF activity, e.g. Logon, Launch, Create, Traffic, Query |
| `severity_id` | int8 | 0 unknown .. 1 info, 2 low, 3 medium, 4 high, 5 critical, 6 fatal |
| `status` | string | Success | Failure | Unknown |
| `product` | string | reporting product, e.g. Microsoft Defender for Endpoint |
| `source` | string | MERIDIAN source key that collected the event |
| `user` | string | normalised user (UPN / e-mail, lower case) |
| `user_domain` | string | user domain |
| `src_ip` | string | source IP |
| `src_port` | int32 | source port |
| `src_country` | string | source country (ISO-2) |
| `dst_ip` | string | destination IP |
| `dst_port` | int32 | destination port |
| `dst_domain` | string | destination host / domain |
| `device` | string | device hostname (lower case FQDN or short name) |
| `device_id` | string | device id from the reporting tool |
| `device_ip` | string | device IP |
| `process_name` | string | process image name |
| `process_cmdline` | string | process command line |
| `parent_process_name` | string | parent process image name |
| `file_name` | string | file name |
| `file_path` | string | file path |
| `file_sha256` | string | file SHA-256 |
| `file_md5` | string | file MD5 |
| `url` | string | URL |
| `http_method` | string | HTTP method |
| `dns_query` | string | DNS query name |
| `action` | string | allowed | blocked | quarantined | ... as reported |
| `auth_protocol` | string | authentication protocol / method |
| `mfa` | bool | multi-factor satisfied |
| `app_name` | string | application / service principal name |
| `cloud_account` | string | cloud account / subscription / tenant |
| `cloud_region` | string | cloud region |
| `api_operation` | string | API operation, e.g. StopLogging, Add member to role |
| `resource` | string | target resource |
| `message` | string | human-readable summary |
| `tags` | string | ; separated tags (asset criticality, crown_jewel, ioc ...) |
| `ioc_hits` | string | ; separated threat-intel indicators matched at ingestion |
| `event_uid` | string | stable event id (de-duplication) |
| `raw` | string | original record (JSON) for forensics |

## 2. Operational store (PostgreSQL in production, SQLite for local use)

Tables are created at start-up if missing. Every string column except keys truncates at its declared length
(values come from attacker-controlled telemetry).

## 3. State machines

### Alert

`new` -> (triage) -> `closed` (benign, auto-close gate passed) | `triaged` (kept for a human / joined to a case) |
`needs_human` (agent run failed or hit a limit)

### Case

`new` / `triaged` -> `investigating` -> `awaiting_approval` (containment requested) -> `contained` (action executed) -> `closed`;
a rejected request returns the case to `investigating`.

### Approval

`pending` -> `approved` -> `executed` | `failed`; or `pending` -> `rejected`; or `pending` -> `expired` (TTL,
default 24 h). The transition out of `pending` is atomic, so an approval executes at most once.

### Work item

`queued` -> `running` (leased, 3600 s for agents) -> `done` | `failed` (after max attempts) ; an expired lease
returns the item to the queue.
